calls.head: Thompson gets company tonight
calls.body: At home, the Capitals keep sending Tuch’s line (Protas, Dubois and Tuch) out against opponents’ first lines, far more often than chance would suggest. Spencer Carbery has been giving this group the hard job of facing the other team’s top line. Tonight the Sabres’ first line is Benson, Kulich and Thompson.

calls.head: Thompson is due against the Sabres
calls.body: Since 2023-24, Thompson has been shaky against the Sabres, well below his usual. Fans love a pattern like this, but we checked three seasons of them and they predicted nothing. Don’t be surprised if he’s back to his usual self.

surprises.head: Washington’s power play came alive
surprises.body: Washington’s power play created 19.2 expected goals per 60, against their usual 7.0 (about 7.4 against Buffalo) and a league average of 7.7. A team strays this far about once every 90 games.

story.head: Ovechkin sets the Capitals’ assists record
paras: The Sabres scored four times in the first. Tom Wilson and Sam Carrick opened the game with a fight, and Jack Quinn got the scoring started for the Sabres early in the first. Rasmus Dahlin made it 2-0 on the power play less than five minutes later. Beck Malenstyn stretched the lead to 3-0, 25 seconds later. Washington pulled Logan Thompson after three goals and turned to Charlie Lindgren for the rest of the first. Alex Tuch got the Capitals on the board midway through the first, and Zach Benson pushed the lead to 4-1 late in the period. Tage Thompson made it 5-1 on the power play with just nine seconds left in the second. Ryan Leonard cut Buffalo’s lead to 5-2 on the power play midway through the third, his fourth straight game with a goal. Boone Jenner made it 5-3, 52 seconds later, and Quinn scored his second of the night into the empty net with 43 seconds left. Quinn added an assist for a three-point night.

The score flatters the Sabres: the Capitals had the better of the chances. Replay those chances a hundred times and the Capitals win about six in ten. Ukko-Pekka Luukkonen, who gave up five goals against Tampa Bay in his last start, made 34 saves for the Sabres. The Sabres improved to 9-9-4, sixth in the Atlantic, while the Caps fell to 10-10-0, slipping to sixth in the Metropolitan.

items.text: Alex Ovechkin passed Nicklas Bäckström to become the Capitals’ all-time leader in assists, with 763.
The Sabres won for the first time in six games.
The Capitals are on a four-game losing streak.
Aliaksei Protas has a point in six straight games.
